accepted.s: Which work was written by Gopal Hari Deshmukh under the pen name ‘Lokahitawadi’?
accepted.x: Gopal Hari Deshmukh wrote Shatapatre, meaning ‘hundred letters’, in the weekly Prabhakar under the pen name Lokahitawadi.
accepted.tq: Use the exact work–reformer association and distinguish it from nearby journals.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the Prarthana Samaj, Widow Remarriage Association, Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Deccan Education Society and National Social Conference?
accepted.x: Justice M.G. Ranade was associated with all the listed reform organisations and bodies. He also advocated the close connection between religious and social reform.
accepted.tq: Identify the reformer from a cluster of institutional associations.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Justice M.G. Ranade’s views:
1. Rigid religious belief obstructs social, economic and political progress.
2. Social reform and religious reform should be treated as unrelated spheres.
3. Social and religious reform should proceed together.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Ranade held that rigid religious belief obstructed progress and that social and religious reform were interrelated. Statement 2 is false because he did not regard them as unrelated.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reformer’s central argument.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s: R.G. Bhandarkar, associated with the Prarthana Samaj, was primarily known as a—
accepted.x: R.G. Bhandarkar was known as a Sanskrit scholar and joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870.
accepted.tq: Test a precise biographical description rather than a broad organisational association.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s: In which year did R.G. Bhandarkar join the Prarthana Samaj?
accepted.x: R.G. Bhandarkar joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related reform dates by focusing on the event attached to the year.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s: Who started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832?
accepted.x: Bal Shastri Jambhekar started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832 and attacked Brahmanical orthodoxy.
accepted.tq: Match the journal with its reformer and use the associated year as confirmation.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reformers → title/pen name and body

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was established in 1873 at Pune. The other pairs contain incorrect years or places.
accepted.tq: Start from the pair containing both the correct year and location.
accepted.sec: Reform body → founder

accepted.s:
Arrange the following reform bodies in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Prarthana Samaj
B. Paramahansa Mandali
C. Satyashodhak Samaj
D. Arya Samaj
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded in 1849, Prarthana Samaj in 1867, Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 and Arya Samaj in 1875.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then arrange the middle events.
accepted.sec: Reform body → founder

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Young Bengal Movement — Henry Louis Vivian Derozio
accepted.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule, not Dayananda Saraswati. Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped founder among otherwise familiar reform organisations.
accepted.sec: Reform body → founder

accepted.s: Paramahansa Mandali was primarily characterised as a—
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali was a secret society concerned with religious and social reform.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organisational nature of a reform body from its aims.
accepted.sec: Paramahansa Mandali - year, city, nature, aims, founders

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Paramahansa Mandali:
1. It advocated belief in one God.
2. It opposed caste discrimination.
3. It supported women’s education and widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali advocated belief in one God, opposed caste discrimination, and supported women’s education and widow remarriage.
accepted.tq: Combine the body’s religious principle with its social-reform objectives.
accepted.sec: Paramahansa Mandali - year, city, nature, aims, founders

accepted.s: A practice associated with the members of Paramahansa Mandali was—
o: refusing all forms of education for women
eating food cooked by members of lower castes
promoting idol worship as its central doctrine
accepted.x: Members of Paramahansa Mandali broke caste rules by eating food cooked by members of lower castes.
accepted.tq: Apply the organisation’s anti-caste principle to a concrete social practice.
accepted.sec: Paramahansa Mandali - year, city, nature, aims, founders

accepted.s: Who were associated with the founding of Paramahansa Mandali?
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang along with Durgaram Mancharam of the Manav Dharma Sabha of Surat.
accepted.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and distinguish it from leaders of other reform movements.
accepted.sec: Paramahansa Mandali - year, city, nature, aims, founders

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the location of Paramahansa Mandali?
o: It was founded in Bombay and had branches at Poona and Satara.
It was founded in Pune and had branches only in Bengal.
It was founded in Calcutta and had branches at Bombay and Pune.
It was founded in Surat and had branches at Calcutta and Satara.
accepted.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded in Bombay and had branches at Poona and Satara. Some accounts refer to its establishment at Poona in 1849 in examination questions.
accepted.tq: Separate the founding city from the cities where branches were established.
accepted.sec: Paramahansa Mandali - year, city, nature, aims, founders

accepted.s: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was a teacher at which institution?
accepted.x: Derozio was a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, where he influenced the Young Bengal Movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the movement through its institutional centre.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio belonged to which background?
accepted.x: Derozio was of Anglo-Indian, or Indo-Portuguese, descent.
accepted.tq: Test the leader’s exact nationality or community background rather than his place of work.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: The Young Bengal Movement was particularly inspired by the—
accepted.x: The ideas of the Young Bengal Movement were inspired by the French Revolution and its emphasis on reason and liberty.
accepted.tq: Link the intellectual movement with its stated historical inspiration.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Henry Vivian Derozio:
1. He was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831.
2. He died in 1831.
3. He continued as a teacher at Hindu College until 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831 and died in the same year. Statement 3 is false because he did not continue there until 1857.
accepted.tq: Use the paired date facts and reject the exaggerated continuation of service.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a characteristic of the ideas associated with the Young Bengal Movement?
o: Support for women’s rights and education
accepted.x: Young Bengal thinkers attacked old traditions and decadent customs rather than defending them uncritically. The movement was radical, rationalist and iconoclastic and supported women’s rights and education.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that reverses the movement’s reformist and rationalist outlook.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: The followers of Henry Derozio were known as the—
accepted.x: Derozio’s followers were known as the Derozians, and their forum was the Academic Association.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a movement’s followers from the names of other reform organisations.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: The forum associated with the followers of Derozio was the—
accepted.x: The Derozians used the Academic Association as their forum for discussion and intellectual activity.
accepted.tq: Match the movement’s followers with their specific forum.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - college, leader's nationality, ideas, followers

accepted.s: Prarthana Samaj emerged as—
o: an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj and a reform movement within Hinduism
a Christian missionary society founded in Pune
a political organisation formed by the Indian National Congress
a branch of the Arya Samaj opposed to all social reform
accepted.x: Prarthana Samaj was an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj and functioned as a reform movement within Hinduism.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional relationship and reject nearby but incorrect reform traditions.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s: The establishment of Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867 was influenced by the visit of—
accepted.x: Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the visit of Keshab Chandra Sen and was established in Bombay in 1867.
accepted.tq: Use the inspiration–organisation association rather than confusing different reform leaders.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s: Who were the principal leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra?
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar were prominent leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct leadership pair instead of its founder alone.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the four-point social agenda of the Prarthana Samaj?
accepted.x: The four-point agenda included opposition to the caste system, women’s education, widow remarriage, and raising the age of marriage for men and women. Compulsory conversion to Christianity was not part of it.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated religious demand among the organisation’s social objectives.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prarthana Samaj:
1. It worked through persuasion and social work rather than confrontation.
2. Its activities included support for inter-dining and inter-marriage.
3. It sought the uplift of depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Prarthana Samaj pursued reform through persuasion and social work and also supported inter-dining, inter-marriage and the uplift of depressed classes.
accepted.tq: Combine the organisation’s method of reform with its additional social objectives.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s: Which statement best distinguishes the Prarthana Samaj from the Brahmo Samaj in the context of social reform?
o: Prarthana Samaj focused mainly on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste practices.
Prarthana Samaj completely rejected all forms of social reform.
Prarthana Samaj was exclusively a political body with no religious connection.
Prarthana Samaj required the abandonment of Hindu society before permitting reform.
accepted.x: The exam-safe distinction is that Prarthana Samaj focused more on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste in the manner described for the Brahmos.
accepted.tq: Compare the practical social emphasis of two related reform traditions without using an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Prarthana Samaj - year, place, inspiration, four-point agenda

accepted.s: The National Social Conference was founded in 1887 mainly because—
o: the Young Bengal Movement had shifted its headquarters to Pune
the Arya Samaj refused to discuss educational questions
the Prarthana Samaj had been dissolved by the colonial government
the Indian National Congress concentrated on political issues and did not adequately address social reform
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade founded the National Social Conference with Raghunath Rao because the Congress largely confined itself to political issues. The Conference provided a forum for social reform.
accepted.tq: Test the cause behind the creation of an organisation rather than merely its date.
accepted.sec: National Social Conference - founder and reason

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Social Conference:
1. It was founded by M.G. Ranade with Raghunath Rao.
2. It met at the same time and place as the sessions of the Indian National Congress.
3. It was created to discuss social reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The National Social Conference was founded in 1887 and met alongside the Congress to discuss social reform.
accepted.tq: Verify founder, institutional arrangement and purpose together.
accepted.sec: National Social Conference - founder and reason

accepted.s: The Widow Remarriage Association associated with M.G. Ranade was established in—
accepted.x: The Widow Remarriage Association associated with M.G. Ranade was established in 1861.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of an associated institution from the years of later reform bodies.
accepted.sec: Institutions linked - Widow Remarriage Association, Deccan Education Society

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the Deccan Education Society?
o: Founded in 1884 at Pune by Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar, with Ranade’s support
Founded in 1861 at Bombay by Ranade and Bhandarkar without other associates
Founded in 1873 at Pune by Jyotiba Phule and Derozio
Founded in 1887 at Calcutta by Raghunath Rao and Keshab Chandra Sen
accepted.x: The Deccan Education Society was founded in Pune in 1884 by Tilak, Agarkar, Chiplunkar and others, with the support of M.G. Ranade.
accepted.tq: Check the institution through its year, place, founders and supporter together.
accepted.sec: Institutions linked - Widow Remarriage Association, Deccan Education Society

accepted.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, associated with M.G. Ranade, was established in—
accepted.x: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was established in 1870 and was associated with M.G. Ranade.
accepted.tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates by linking each year to its organisation.
accepted.sec: Institutions linked - Widow Remarriage Association, Deccan Education Society

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Induprakash, an Anglo-Marathi journal, was linked to M.G. Ranade. Prabhakar carried Deshmukh’s Shatapatre, Darpan was started by Jambhekar, and Dnyanodaya was a Marathi Christian missionary journal.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure journal–reformer pair and eliminate the swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Journals → reformer

accepted.s: Prabhakar was the weekly that carried—
accepted.x: Prabhakar carried Gopal Hari Deshmukh’s Shatapatre, or ‘hundred letters’.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a journal from the work published in it.
accepted.sec: Journals → reformer

accepted.s: Dnyanodaya was associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: Dnyanodaya was a Marathi Christian missionary journal associated with the American Marathi Mission.
accepted.tq: Identify the journal through its institutional publisher rather than a social reformer.
accepted.sec: Journals → reformer
